scope: source read-only; evidence-only independent probes; no crate/Cargo/tracking edits

findings.trigger: Large manifest, many tiny files, or up to 64 simultaneous large reads.
original_evidence: evidence/small-libs-batch-01/tg-package-integrity/0x14067c3d0.c: one easy-parallel each/run across all entries
Original and candidate easy-parallel 3.2.0 lib.rs Parallel::run/finish: one spawned thread for every closure except the final caller-thread closure
findings.actual_reproduction: perf-results.json: 1792 repeated zero-byte entries 109.601 ms; 64 entries reading the same 2 MiB file 37.890 ms with peak working set 22,327,296 bytes vs baseline 3,395,584. All returned Ok. Existing dev-profile library, optimized harness, one run per workload, cached repeated-file synthetic workload, not original-run or production throughput.
findings.impact: Batching reduces live spawned-thread ceiling to 63, but creates N-ceil(N/64) new threads across the full run (1764 at N=1792 vs original 1791). Reads materialize every live file: time O(total read bytes + directory entries + N thread startups); extra memory O(sum sizes of live reads + names/issues), not bounded independently of file sizes. No demonstrated regression or pathological slowdown.
findings.suggestion: Keep 64 batch as acceptable scoped choice. Before high-frequency use, benchmark real release consumer; if needed use a persistent pool from an already original-locked dependency (rayon only after lock/source/features audit), and blake3::Hasher::update_reader / std buffered IO for streaming. Preserve Missing on any read failure and ordered duplicate results.
findings.resolution: Optional optimization; no business-policy change requested by this review.

findings.trigger: Actual game integrity report or crash reporter attempts to consume verification result.
original_evidence: skeleton/B/crates/tg-package-integrity/src/lib.rs: direct callers tiny_glade::integrity_report_main::verify_package_integrity_and_show_report at RVA 0x2552f5 and tiny_glade::panic_reporter::panic_report::on_game_crashed at RVA 0x3b040f
findings.actual_reproduction: consumer-search.txt: bounded search across shared-foundation Rust finds only library/tests/inspect_package example, no recovered game report/crash consumer. probe-result.txt verifies candidate enum categories on controlled disk; original full verify/report entry was not executed.
findings.impact: Core library policy is callable, but cannot yet claim full original game business closure or error-report compatibility. This is an integration/acceptance gap, not evidence of a library algorithm bug.
findings.suggestion: Restore one real original consumer using the root/paths owner, map new enum to report semantics and implement local report output. Validate read/checksum/parse/version/missing/corrupt/extra through this shared consumer. Do not send reports during validation.
findings.resolution: Remaining work outside current core library scope.

findings.trigger: Unknown fields, sequence-form struct, duplicate or missing fields, negative/overflow/floating version, malformed tuple.
original_evidence: skeleton/B/crates/tg-package-integrity/src/lib.rs: PackageManifest serde derive deserialize/visit_map/visit_seq symbols and tuple(String,String), serde u32 monomorph references
findings.actual_reproduction: probe-result.txt: gated raw JSON accepts unknown_field and sequence_form; rejects u32_overflow, negative_version, float_version, duplicate_version, missing_files and one-element tuple as ManifestParse. These are candidate runtime observations; matching exact original serde attributes/accepted input set remains unproved. Independent original-review MCP failed before ready state, not a parser result.
findings.impact: Main shipped schema works. Rare accepted/rejected schema set cannot yet be called fully compatible; no confirmed mismatch, and PDB visit_seq makes candidate sequence support plausible rather than suspicious.
findings.suggestion: Use focused original parser/visitor control-flow or controlled original entry oracle to verify the listed input classes. Keep serde 1.0.200 and serde_json 1.0.85; do not hand-write validators or parser to guess stricter behavior.
findings.resolution: Unknown retained, not classified as a bug.

findings.trigger: OS thread creation failure or a worker panic while Parallel::finish is spawning/collecting jobs.
original_evidence: easy-parallel 3.2.0 lib.rs: thread::spawn plus NoPanic guard aborts process if unwinding during startup; normal worker panic resumes after joining
Original entry directly uses same easy-parallel dependency
findings.actual_reproduction: No system exhaustion or panic injection performed; normal 134-outcome cross-batch probe preserves all Missing entries and ordered Corrupt results. Thread-exhaustion behavior is established from the reused dependency source, not original or candidate fault-injection runtime.
findings.impact: Public Result does not encompass all operational failures: resource exhaustion can terminate process. Same mechanism exists in original; candidate batching lowers live demand. No evidence this is newly introduced or relevant to the observed package.
findings.suggestion: Document inherited operational boundary. If used in a resilient tool or frequent consumer, prefer an existing audited persistent pool or controlled sequential fallback; evaluate behavior change explicitly.

findings.trigger: Root selection differs from original CWD or files change during verification.
original_evidence: evidence/small-libs-batch-01/tg-package-integrity/0x14067c3d0.c: fixed CWD manifest and one Parallel run
findings.actual_reproduction: Explicit isolated root probes, exact self path, duplicates, root tmp/nested tmp and ordered aggregation all pass. Concurrent mutation schedule not compared.
findings.impact: Root parameter is a useful interface representation and 64 batches limit concurrency. File mutation timing can differ, so stable-filesystem scope must remain explicit.
findings.suggestion: Keep these choices; consumer must select the original package root. Do not label batching or readable error enum names a defect solely for non-1:1 implementation.

findings.trigger: Porting B package verifier to 32-bit or big-endian target, or future std Hash encoding changes.
findings.actual_reproduction: 4096 original x64 hash-leaf inputs and 128 raw-byte checksum compositions match candidate on current Windows x64. Other architectures not compiled/executed.
findings.impact: std Hash array prefix depends on host usize/encoding; current B host is verified, general portable format promise is not. No current B bug.
findings.suggestion: If cross-host support is intended, encode the evidenced 32u64 little-endian prefix then digest bytes through the same fnv Hasher dependency instead of relying on native array Hash; this is policy composition, not a custom FNV implementation.
findings.resolution: Current baseline limited to B Windows x86_64.
